doc.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Brazil every year: favelas, gangsters who play and Carnival
summary: Jones describes going to Brazil every year for 54 years, the favelas, the musicians who are also gangsters, Gilberto Gil, and urges Baker to come to Carnival.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: . . . and blues. Ask the Stones. All the hip-hoppers are coming to me now to talk about, “I want to be a good musician.” Before they were saying, “Hip-hop is where it’s happening.” I know it is, and I love hip-hop. You know I’m the biggest supporter out there. But I said, guess what? I just got back from Brazil. I go to Brazil every year for 54 years. We’re doing a film down there next year for the favelas and Katrina. I’m going to take the musicians from blues and jazz, a float for each one. We [?] talk [?]. I’ve been down there a long time. I go every year. We use the money to help the favelas. I saw them start in 1956 with D[?] at 3,000 kids and no parents. Now it’s 600,000. I go every year, because these cats are gangsters, but they’re my buddies. Come on now. Get in queue before 4, because we start slingin’ dope at 4. You get there, and they play for you, and they’re humble and polite. The guys play. The Afro-reggae guys play. Coming out, they’re cleaning their AK-47s. The army can’t go in there. The helicopters [?]. These cats don’t play. They’ve got in perfect in Bahia, El Salvador, because [Colinius?] Brown’s got them and told them, it’s drums, not guns. No dope and no violence. Gilberto Gil’s the minister of culture. I’ve known him 45 years. One of the best musicians in the world, singers and guitar players. Unbelievable. What a culture. Have you been to Brazil?
David Baker, however you do it, try to find a way to get down there February 2nd. You have never experienced anything like that in your life, like the carnival. I promise
